Definition
[Hyperboloid model] \group modelsSource: thurston:page-0025, thurston:page-0026, thurston:page-0027 On $\R ^{n+1}$ use $Q(X)=X_1^2+\cdots +X_n^2-X_{n+1}^2$. The positive sheet $H^n=\{ Q=-1,X_{n+1}>0\} $, with the restricted form, is hyperbolic space of curvature $-1$. Planes through the origin meet it in geodesics. Projection from the origin gives the projective model, and projective transformations preserving the sphere at infinity are induced by isometries of $Q$; hence hyperbolic space has no non-isometric similarities.
